protections: Inline config overrides of a transport protocol are refused: a `-c` argument whose following value matches `protocol[.<name>].allow` is rejected with a GitPluginError unless the instance was built with `unsafe.allowUnsafeProtocolOverride` (simple-git/src/lib/plugins/block-unsafe-operations-plugin.ts:10-24, applied to every spawn at simple-git/src/lib/plugins/block-unsafe-operations-plugin.ts:31-38, registered for all instances at simple-git/src/lib/git-factory.ts:59).

A caller-supplied remote pack program is refused for clone and fetch only: a task command list containing `--upload-pack` or `--upload-pack=<value>` becomes a configuration error instead of a spawn (simple-git/src/lib/tasks/clone.ts:32-34 with lookup at :46-49; simple-git/src/lib/tasks/fetch.ts:7-9 with lookup at :21-24).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: `git pull` is git's own porcelain over fetch, so the existing fetch guard looks like it covers this route; in fact pullTask builds its own command list from the caller's options and never calls fetchTask, so a `--upload-pack` value is passed to `git pull` verbatim.

`raw` is documented as 'executes any command against the git binary' and the unsafe-actions guide puts the burden on the caller to validate user input before calling simple-git (docs/PLUGIN-UNSAFE-ACTIONS.md:3-7), so an unsafe option reaching a `raw` spawn looks like intended behaviour rather than a missing guard; the only shared check raw meets is the `-c protocol...` one, which says nothing about pack programs.

push only sends objects, so a pack option looks unrelated to the clone/fetch upload-pack guards; `--receive-pack` (and its documented alias `--exec`) name the program run on the receiving side, which a solver can assume is the remote's problem even though a file:// push runs it locally.

clone already rejects `--upload-pack`, so the protection looks present and done; the check is a regex on the long spelling only, and `git clone -u <upload-pack>` is the documented short form of the same option, so the shape is not covered.
`ls-remote` only lists refs, so no pack is transferred and the upload-pack guards look irrelevant; the command still accepts `--upload-pack`, which names the program the listing is served by.

the protocol guard already refuses `-c protocol.<name>.allow`, and clone's `--config` option is documented and used for benign values such as `http.extraheader` (the library's own clone unit test uses it), so the option looks handled; while the check only recognises the exact token `-c`, the long form `--config protocol.ext.allow=always` (and the option-object form `--config=protocol.ext.allow=always` produced by the shared option converter) passes the guard untouched.

the protocol guard is written around `-c`, and `--config-env` is an unrelated-looking top-level switch whose value comes from the environment, while the environment is configured through a separate builder (`.env()`), so the two surfaces look disconnected; a `--config-env=protocol.ext.allow=<ENV>` argument in a `raw` command list is never inspected as a config switch.

masking: The per-task guards in clone.ts:46-49 and fetch.ts:21-24 mask the absence of a shared pack-option guard: tests written against clone and fetch pass, so a solver can conclude the pack surface is covered; only those two commands are checked, and any shared guard that is added later must also cover the short form `-u` once the unconditional per-task checks are relaxed for an opt-in.

conflicts.what: A shared pack-option guard that also has to cover clone's `-u` alias conflicts with the unconditional per-task checks in clone.ts:46-49 and fetch.ts:21-24: if those stay, any opt-in to permit a custom pack program can never take effect for clone/fetch because the task returns a configuration error before spawn, while their existing unit tests assert the old 'potential exploit argument blocked' message (simple-git/test/unit/clone.spec.ts:66, simple-git/test/unit/fetch.spec.ts:75).

The natural over-broad fix for T6 (refuse `--config` / `--config=<value>` outright) breaks the legitimate `--config http.extraheader=...` clone option that the library itself exercises (simple-git/test/unit/clone.spec.ts:30-31); the fix has to recognise the config-switch shape but reject only protocol.*.allow values, the same narrowness the pack-option rule needs at the shared layer.

fairness_risks: `--config http.extraheader=AUTHORIZATION ...` is a legitimate clone option exercised by the project's own unit test (simple-git/test/unit/clone.spec.ts:30-31); a security rule that refuses `--config`/`--config=...` as a shape would contradict that must-keep-working behaviour.

A custom upload-pack/receive-pack program is a legitimate need (mirrors, non-standard remote installations, restricted networks); refusing the option outright rather than offering an explicit opt-in contradicts it.

`git.raw` is documented as an arbitrary git passthrough (simple-git/src/git.js:356-381) and the unsafe-actions guide places input validation on the caller (docs/PLUGIN-UNSAFE-ACTIONS.md:3-7); a shared rule that refuses `--upload-pack`/`--receive-pack` for every spawn changes raw's contract for callers who intentionally manage trusted remotes.

The existing clone/fetch checks are lexical over all command tokens (simple-git/src/lib/tasks/clone.ts:32-34 scans every command at :46; fetch also scans the remote and branch strings at simple-git/src/lib/tasks/fetch.ts:18-21), so a legitimate repo path, URL, branch or remote that happens to begin with `--upload-pack` is refused even when a `--` separator would make it positional.
Blocking clone's `-u` short option removes a documented git flag that legitimate users may need for a non-standard remote git installation, so the rule has to be paired with an opt-in.

design.why: Three independent guards have to be written, each with a different reason to dismiss. (1) One shared spawn-args guard for caller-supplied pack programs; T1 (pull), T3 (push/--receive-pack) and T5 (ls-remote) are the same guard seen from other entry points, and T2 (raw) is its hardest, most dismissible route: the docs tell callers to validate their own input and raw is explicitly an arbitrary passthrough (docs/PLUGIN-UNSAFE-ACTIONS.md:3-7), which is the absent-protection-plus-reason-to-dismiss shape DeepSeek misses. (2) The clone short-alias shape (T4): the existing clone guard matches only the long spelling while `-u` is the same option, so a solver who copies the current regex leaves it open; this is the how-type/shape judgement MiMo tends to miss. (3) The long-form config switch (T6/T7): the protocol guard recognises only the exact token `-c`, while clone's `--config`, the option-object form `--config=<key>=<value>`, and `--config-env` all carry the same protocol.*.allow value, next to a must-keep-working `--config http.extraheader` value the project itself exercises; this is the coupled-value judgement MiMo over-hardens on. The three groups sit at different layers (shared spawn args, one command's option alias, the protocol config-switch check), so a fix for one does not close the others, and each needs a separate decision from the pinned code.

unverified: The text of GHSA-9w5j-4mwv-2wj8 and the diff of the published fix ec97a39ab60b could not be read from the pinned tree (no advisory text or network access is available here). The identification of the later bug with the caller-supplied pack-program gap (T1/T2/T3/T5) is inferred from the pinned plugin's shape (it refuses only protocol overrides, and its spawn.args action receives the command context at simple-git/src/lib/plugins/block-unsafe-operations-plugin.ts:31 but ignores it) together with the pre-existing clone/fetch-only upload-pack guards; if the published fix instead only widened the protocol config-switch check, then the T6/T7 group is the later bug and the pack routes are the uncovered ones. Either way the trap locations are real in the pinned code.

That `git clone --config protocol.ext.allow=always` writes the setting before the remote history is fetched is git CLI behaviour (the repo only shows the option being passed through, simple-git/test/unit/clone.spec.ts:30-31), not verified inside this repository.

That `git pull` forwards `--upload-pack` to its fetch phase and that `git ls-remote --upload-pack`, `git clone -u`, `git push --receive-pack` and `git push --exec` select the program that is run are git CLI semantics; the repository only shows that simple-git passes the caller's tokens through (pull.ts:12, remote.ts:27, clone.ts:41-46, push.ts:14).

`--exec` is a documented alias for push's `--receive-pack`; it is listed inside T3 rather than as its own trap because it is the same sink and the same guard, and the repository has no test or reference for it.

Case variants such as `-c Protocol.ext.allow=always` and `-c protocol.ext.Allow=always` appear to bypass the guard's case-sensitive regex, but they are pure spelling variants and are deliberately not recorded as traps (also not verifiable here without running git).

Written/programmatic config (`git.addConfig('protocol.ext.allow', 'always')`, simple-git/src/lib/tasks/config.ts:24-45) is not treated as a trap: it is a deliberate config-management API, not an inline spawn argument, and it is outside the stated protection.

Whether the published fix also relaxed or removed the unconditional clone/fetch task-level checks (needed to make a pack opt-in work for those two commands) is unknown from the pinned tree; the conflict recorded above is the interaction a solver would hit either way.
